mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% within the prior 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 4 consecutive months with monthly YoM change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand collapse, which depresses earnings and cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall by >1% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for six consecutive months signals a deep labor market downturn, which consistently reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its prior 12-month high signals a resumption of demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during recovery regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.
